title: The rigidified Picard scheme of a smooth projective variety
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically integral scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and let $e\in X(k)$. The functor on $k$-schemes $T$ of invertible sheaves $M$ on $X\times_kT$ [def-sc-invertible-module] equipped with an isomorphism $M|_{e\times T}\cong\mathcal O_T$, modulo isomorphisms respecting this rigidification, is represented by a separated commutative group scheme $P$ locally of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Tensor product defines its group law. Its identity component $P^0$ is an open and closed, proper connected subgroup scheme of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A map $T\to P$ factors through $P^0$ exactly when every geometric fibre of its line bundle is algebraically equivalent to the trivial bundle. Here algebraic equivalence is the equivalence relation generated by pairs of fibres in an invertible-sheaf family over a connected smooth parameter variety. There is a universal invertible sheaf on $X\times P$, with its rigidification along $e\times P$, whose restriction to $X\times\{0\}$ is trivial. Finally, the tangent space $T_0P^0$, defined as the dual of the maximal ideal modulo its square in the local ring at $0$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], is canonically $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$, the first Zariski sheaf cohomology of the structure sheaf [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. No smoothness or reducedness of $P^0$ is asserted.

proof.text: Write $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The proper geometrically integral global-functions theorem gives $f_*\mathcal O_X=k$. Every $k$-scheme $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat; apply flat base change in degree zero to obtain the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_T\simeq(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}$. Smoothness supplies flatness and local finite presentation, and projectivity supplies properness and quasi-compactness; hence $f$ is flat, proper and finitely presented, as required below.

Apply the split Picard sequence to the section $e_T$. It identifies $\operatorname{Pic}_{X/k}(T)$ with $\ker(e_T^*:\operatorname{Pic}(X_T)\to\operatorname{Pic}(T))$. Normalize a bundle $L$ by $L\otimes f_T^*(e_T^*L)^{-1}$; its section pullback has the canonical trivialization. Any two trivializations of a normalized bundle differ by a unit of $T$, which acts on the bundle by the same scalar because $(f_T)_*\mathcal O_{X_T}=\mathcal O_T$. Thus normalized classes are exactly isomorphism classes of rigidified bundles, naturally in $T$. A rigidification-preserving automorphism is a scalar whose restriction to $e_T$ is $1$, hence is the identity.

The general flat proper Picard theorem gives an algebraic space $P$ locally of finite presentation over $k$, with immersion diagonal and the tensor-product commutative group law. Its immersion diagonal makes it locally separated. The group-space theorem therefore makes $P$ a separated scheme locally of finite type over $k$. Step 2 identifies its functor with the requested rigidified functor, with the same tensor-product operation.

Evaluate the representing bijection at $T=P$ on $1_P$. Its image is an actual rigidified invertible module $\mathcal U$ on $X\times P$, and naturality says that every classified family is its pullback. The group identity represents the trivial rigidified bundle, so pulling $\mathcal U$ back along $X\times\{0\}$ gives $\mathcal O_X$ with its rigidification. Apply the group-component theorem to $P$: the identity component $P^0$ is an open and closed connected subgroup scheme of finite type, and its formation commutes with field extension.

source.place: Tag 0B7R (proposition-connected-component) and the definition of representation by a functor of points.

proof.text: To prove properness, take any DVR $R$ over $k$, fraction field $K$, and $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to P^0$. The classified rigidified line bundle $L$ on $X_K$ extends to $\widetilde L$ on $X_R$ by the smooth-DVR extension theorem, since $X_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is the base change of the smooth finite-type morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Normalize $\widetilde L$ by tensoring with $f_R^*(e_R^*\widetilde L)^{-1}$. The resulting rigidified bundle restricts to $L$ as a rigidified class by step 2, so it defines $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to P$ extending $a$. The inverse image of $P^0$ is open and closed and contains the generic point. Since $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is connected it is all of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, and $b$ factors through $P^0$. Separatedness gives uniqueness of this extension. The Noetherian DVR criterion now proves $P^0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ proper: its finite-type hypothesis was proved in step 4. This argument does not replace $P^0$ by its reduction.

Over any algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, a family over a connected smooth parameter variety $B/\Omega$ gives a map $B\to P_\Omega$: normalize along $e\times B$ as in step 2. Since $P_\Omega^0$ is open and closed, either all of $B$ maps into it or none does. Consequently every chain generating algebraic equivalence preserves membership in $P_\Omega^0$. Conversely let $p\in P_\Omega^0(\Omega)$. The reduction $B=(P_\Omega^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is a smooth connected integral separated scheme of finite type by the group-component theorem. Both $p$ and $0$ factor through this reduction, since $\Omega$ is reduced. Pull back $\mathcal U$ to $X_\Omega\times B$; its fibres at $p$ and $0$ are the line bundle at $p$ and the trivial bundle. This is a single permitted smooth connected parameter family, so those bundles are algebraically equivalent. For a general $T\to P$, each geometric point of $T$ tests exactly this equivalence. Thus the stated fibre condition says that the image of $T$ is contained in the open subset $P^0$, which is equivalent to factorization through its open immersion.

source.place: Tags 0B7R, 047R, 047N, 047P; agent argument using the universal rigidified family. Compare Kleiman, Proposition 5.10, with the smooth-parameter formulation verified here.

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Spec}k[\epsilon]$ with $\epsilon^2=0$. A $D$-point reducing to $0$ factors through $P^0$ because $D$ has one underlying point. By the rational tangent-cotangent theorem the tangent space defined in the statement is the dual-number tangent space; by representation and step 2 it is the kernel of $\operatorname{Pic}(X_D)\to\operatorname{Pic}(X)$, since every line bundle on the local schemes $D$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is trivial. Indeed local freeness gives a trivializing open neighbourhood of the closed point of a local affine scheme. Such an open contains a basic open $D(u)$ containing the maximal ideal; then $u$ is a unit, so $D(u)$ is the whole scheme and the bundle is trivial. Apply the existing split-thickening Picard-cocycle theorem to identify this kernel with $H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Addition and scalar multiplication agree: tensoring transition units gives $(1+\epsilon a)(1+\epsilon b)=1+\epsilon(a+b)$, and $\epsilon\mapsto c\epsilon$ gives $1+\epsilon ca$. For the square-zero algebra on $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2$, pull the two representing line bundles back by the inclusions of their dual-number algebras and tensor them. This family restricts to the two given tangent vectors, so it is their unique two-parameter lift in the definition of tangent addition; setting both $\epsilon_i=\epsilon$ gives their tensor product. Thus tensor addition is tangent addition. The resulting isomorphism is canonical and $k$-linear; no smoothness of $P^0$ was used.

The item statement is unchanged from the base apart from added definition citations (compared with the base copy in the Q46 snapshots). Steps 1-7 are correct. Step 1: H^0=k by lem-pc-h0 (2), O_T=f_T*O by flat base change in degree 0 because f is qcqs. Step 2: thm-pc-pic-split gives the normalized classes, which equal the rigidified classes (as in quot 0D2A/0D2B). Step 3: Stacks 0D2C/0D2D, plus moduli lemma-pic-functor-qs-lfp for local finite presentation; locally separated implies decent implies separated (08BH), which with 0B8F makes P a scheme. Step 5: properness by the DVR criterion. A generic line bundle extends by 0BD9 (X_R is regular by 036D and its local rings are UFDs by 0AG0), the extension lands in the clopen P^0 because Spec R is connected, and uniqueness comes from separatedness; lem-sfb-noetherian-dvr-properness is used with its stated hypotheses. Step 6: the clopen identity component is compatible with field extension, and (P^0_Ω)_red serves as one parameter family. Step 7: the split-thickening Picard cocycle node plus tangent-cotangent duality give H^1(X,O_X); I checked that addition through the two-parameter lift is the tensor product. The new nodes are true and not duplicates. The flat-proper Picard node generalizes the curve-only lem-sfb-picard-space-curves-smooth. The component node covers locally finite type groups (0B7R, 047R/N/P/L), which the finite-type-only neutral-component-translates node does not.
